description: Implements FORMULATION.md section 4's log-scaled per-feature normalizer n(x) = clip((log10(x+1) - a) / (b - a), 0, 1). Factored out as its own testable unit since it is applied identically to six of the nine complexity features (install size, early-access duration, dev catalog size, achievement count, DLC count, language count) and is exactly the kind of small pure-math function whose boundary behaviour (x=0, x at bound a or b, b==a) needs its own dedicated tests independent of the larger compute_complexity_score composition.
signature: def normalize_feature_log_scaled(x: float, a: float, b: float) -> float
docstring:
Normalize one raw feature value to [0, 1] via a log10 scale.

Args:
    x: Raw feature value, x >= 0 (a count or byte size; log10(x+1) keeps x=0 finite).
    a: Lower normalization bound (on the log10(x+1) scale), from EnrichmentParams.complexity_bounds, typically the run 1 empirical 5th percentile.
    b: Upper normalization bound, typically the run 1 empirical 95th percentile.

Returns:
    clip((log10(x+1) - a) / (b - a), 0, 1).

Raises:
    ValueError: If b == a (degenerate bounds would divide by zero) -- callers (compute_complexity_score) must treat an unfrozen/degenerate bound pair as 'feature not normalizable yet' and route to median imputation instead of calling this function, per EnrichmentParams.complexity_bounds' documented pre-freeze behaviour.
postconditions: Return value is always in [0.0, 1.0] inclusive
Monotonically non-decreasing in x for fixed a, b

edge_cases.expected_behavior: log10(1)=0; result is clip((0-a)/(b-a), 0, 1), typically 0.0 if a<=0

edge_cases.input: x such that log10(x+1) == a exactly
x such that log10(x+1) == b exactly
x far beyond b (an extreme outlier)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: clipped to 1.0, not extrapolated beyond the bound
raises ValueError rather than returning NaN or raising a bare ZeroDivisionError

edge_cases.input: x negative (should not occur for the features this is applied to)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: ValueError -- defensively rejected rather than silently producing a negative log argument error

unit_tests.name: test_clips_at_zero_and_one
unit_tests.description: Values at and beyond a and b clip exactly to 0.0 and 1.0.

unit_tests.name: test_midpoint_value
unit_tests.description: A value exactly halfway between a and b on the log scale returns 0.5.
